sampling_model.design: One random sample of \(n\) independent bounded-window vectors; causal randomness and inferential sampling randomness are kept distinct.
sampling_model.units: Each unit contributes one binary vector in \(\{0,1\}^{\mathcal W_H}\).
sampling_model.treatment: The focal treatment is \(X_{-\gamma}\); the causal estimand compares two interventions while fixing the common possible-parent set \(Z\) at \(z\).
sampling_model.overlap: The collapse and strict-separation results use a strictly positive observed-window law; the general sharp compiler, empty-fiber certification, and confidence-fiber program permit probability-simplex boundary cells.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The multinomial vector \(p\) is estimated by \(\widehat p\); all causal endpoints and same-SCM pairwise contrasts are reoptimized over one simultaneous rational box-simplex region.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their controlled-effect theorem identifies the micro CDE by the conditional-mean adjustment contrast when the outcome is in no nontrivial directed cycle and has no bidirected edge to a directed ancestor.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Theorem 3 identifies under the exact bounded-window micro-ancestry condition; the \(H=L=1\) summary \(B\to X\to Y\), \(Y\leftrightarrow B\) witness satisfies the new condition while violating the label-level summary-ancestor exclusion.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their response-function construction turns one specified discrete causal model into a polynomial program and obtains numerical valid bounds converging to sharpness.

Their causal-order linear program optimizes counterfactual queries over arbitrary masses on complete deterministic response signatures consistent with the supplied order and reconstructs attaining SCMs.
Proposition 3.1 preserves a canonical-domain linear program by pushing an unrestricted simplex mass to equivalence cells and selecting one raw representative per cell for the reverse lift.
Their bounded-segment theorem decides identification in one known periodic bounded-lag ADMG by cutting repeated hedge states.
Their PAG procedure gives sound analytical bounds at least as tight as natural bounds and shows that several graph representatives may remain necessary.
Their covering-collection construction gives uniformly valid minimum-average-volume confidence regions for a multinomial parameter.
Their root-cause method compares identified direct effects under an acyclic causally sufficient summary graph.
Their real-quantifier-elimination algorithm separates combinatorial and algebraic complexity in polynomial count, degree, coefficient height, and variable blocks.

body.tldr: A finite binary process is observed through a bounded window and a lag-abstracted directed and bidirected summary graph. Directed effects occur only at positive lags through \(L\), while bidirected dependence may span any summary-compatible pair of time points in the observed \(H\)-window. The sharp controlled-micro-direct-effect envelope is the attained range of a finite union of raw semi-Markovian response-function polynomial programs, and a total exact certifier returns incompatibility certificates or isolated algebraic endpoints with attaining SCMs. Positive lags make \(Y_0\) terminal, so controlling its full possible-parent set identifies the effect by the Ferreira--Assaad adjustment contrast whenever no admissible endpoint paired bidirectedly with \(Y_0\) lies in the reflexive ancestry of that parent set in the bounded positive-lag supergraph. This exact micro condition permits directed summary cycles through \(Y\) and strictly improves the label-level summary-ancestor exclusion, as witnessed by the one-lag summary \(B\to X\to Y\), \(Y\leftrightarrow B\). The envelope is strictly narrower on a relative-open temporal-instrument family than a complete temporal-order comparator. Simultaneous multinomial regions support tie-aware inference. Exact analysis of the response-signature quotient supplies a general factor-incidence test and a quotient-size bound, while an explicit edge-latent-chain certificate shows that unrestricted quotient-simplex masses can enlarge the independent-edge-latent image; the endpoint compiler therefore retains the raw product parameterization in general.

project_justification.gap: Existing summary-graph adjustment conditions are formulated at label level for models that may contain contemporaneous arrows and general joint exogenous laws. They do not isolate which time-stamped endpoint of a latent incident to terminal \(Y_0\) can actually enter the recursive determination of the controlled possible-parent vector in a bounded positive-lag window. Existing automated bounds take one fixed graph, and unrestricted response-signature quotient simplexes need not preserve nonlinear independent-edge-latent product images.
project_justification.niche: The positive-directed-lag bound makes the full-time refinement set finite and makes the end-of-window outcome terminal, while summary-compatible bidirected lags remain unrestricted inside the observed window. The bounded positive-lag supergraph gives an exact finite-window ancestry test for overlap between the terminal outcome latent block and the controlled possible-parent recursion. Binary canonical response functions turn each fixed-refinement image into a compact semialgebraic set, and the complete temporal-order common-latent model supplies a coherent graph-free outer comparator.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies a sharp raw compiler and a total exact certifier; proves adjustment and envelope collapse under the exact bounded-window micro-ancestry condition; and exhibits the strict-gain one-lag summary \(B\to X\to Y\), \(Y\leftrightarrow B\), which the former label-level condition rejects even though its only \(B\to X\) placement cannot affect controlled parent \(X_{-1}\). It also permits directed summary cycles through the outcome label and embeds every refinement into the complete order-only comparator. Explicit rational primal tables, pointwise dual inequalities, and an interior ledger certify relative-open strict tightening. One multinomial event is propagated through all queries and contrasts. For response-signature compression, the project proves exact factorized push-forward fidelity, gives a necessary-and-sufficient real-algebraic factor-incidence test and a quotient-size bound, and exhibits an exact separating certificate showing why unrestricted quotient-simplex masses cannot replace the raw product parameterization in general.

body.related_work: Ferreira and Assaad (2026, Theorem 9) provide the summary-graph controlled-micro-direct-effect setup and adjustment expression. In the present finite-window binary semi-Markovian class with mutually independent private and pairwise edge latents, strict positive lags make \(Y_0\) terminal. The relevant exclusion can therefore be stated at the finer time-stamped level: no admissible endpoint paired bidirectedly with \(Y_0\) may lie in the reflexive ancestry of the controlled possible-parent set in the bounded positive-lag supergraph. This condition removes both the singleton strongly connected component requirement and the conservative exclusion of every summary bidirected edge to a summary ancestor. The gain is strict: with \(H=L=1\), summary arrows \(B\to X\to Y\), and \(Y\leftrightarrow B\), the sole \(B_{-1}\to X_0\) placement is too late to affect controlled parent \(X_{-1}\), so adjustment holds although \(B\) is a summary ancestor of \(Y\). This is an extension within the present model class, not a claim that the present scope contains Ferreira--Assaad's: they permit contemporaneous arrows and general joint exogenous laws, whereas this paper excludes instantaneous directed effects and imposes independent pairwise-edge-latent factorization. Duarte et al. (2024, Propositions 1--2 and Algorithm 2) provide the canonical response-function and polynomialization method adapted within each refinement; the total exact real-algebraic layer adds branchwise incompatibility certificates, endpoint isolation, causal-size bounds, and decoded SCM witnesses. Jahn, Karnik, and Schulman (2025, Propositions 1--2) inform finite-window reasoning for known bounded-lag periodic ADMGs but are not the source of the present positive-lag restriction. Rossetto and Antonucci (2026) and Choe et al. (2026) motivate quotient programs over unrestricted signature masses. Here exact push-forward preserves the raw image only while the induced factorized quotient family is retained: the edge-latent-chain certificate proves that freeing quotient masses can enlarge the image. A finite factor-incidence sentence decides equality, lexicographic minimization gives a semialgebraic selector when equality holds, and the derived quotient-size bound closes the former size question. Evans (2016, Theorem 4.13 and Proposition 7.4) motivates retaining latent-margin structure. Geiger and Meek (1999) and Basu, Pollack, and Roy (1996) supply the exact-elimination and complexity ancestors. Bellot (2024, Propositions 3--5) shows that partial graphical information can improve graph-free bounds but does not give the present temporal micro-CDE strictness region. Malloy, Tripathy, and Nowak (2020, Theorem 1) motivate whole-multinomial coverage, while Assaad, Ez-Zejjari, and Zan (2023, Proposition 7 and Theorem 1) supply the downstream direct-effect root-cause comparison made uncertainty-aware by the same-SCM tie rule.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Exact push-forward to response-signature equivalence classes preserves the raw image when the induced factorized quotient family is retained, but this operation alone does not reduce the latent product parameterization. The unrestricted branchwise quotient simplex is computationally smaller but is not sound in general: on the six-window-vertex edge-latent-chain instance it contains a rational point violating an observational independence polynomial that vanishes on the raw image. The exact factor-incidence test decides graph by graph whether the unrestricted quotient happens to be safe, and the canonical catalogue has a derived finite quotient-size bound. Consequently the certified endpoint compiler retains raw product weights unless that test succeeds; the remaining limitation is worst-case combinatorial size, not an unresolved fidelity or size claim.
body.honest_scope: The paper studies finite-window binary SCMs with mutually independent private and pairwise edge latents. It excludes instantaneous directed effects and directed lags beyond \(L\), but places no \(L\)-bound on bidirected lags inside the observed \(H\)-window; Ferreira--Assaad allow contemporaneous arrows and general joint exogenous laws, so the positive-lag adjustment theorem is an extension only within the present distinct scope. The envelope is the smallest closed interval containing all attainable CDE values; the attainable set itself need not be connected. No stationarity or infinite-history reduction is assumed. Exact certification is worst-case singly exponential in the raw response-weight dimension and is a certificate engine, not a polynomial-time method. Empty fibers receive exact branchwise infeasibility certificates; nonempty fibers receive attained algebraic endpoints and decoded SCMs. Every graph refinement embeds in the complete temporal-order common-latent comparator, but unrestricted comparator masses are not asserted to respect missing bidirected edges. Strict tightening is relative to positive laws with a nonempty summary-graph fiber. The quotient question is resolved rather than left open: factorized push-forward is exact, a necessary-and-sufficient real-algebraic test characterizes when the unrestricted quotient simplex is also exact, a finite quotient-size bound is proved, and the edge-latent-chain witness shows that unrestricted quotienting fails in general. Accordingly the main compiler remains unquotiented unless the exact test certifies a particular graph. When the refinement class is a singleton the construction reduces to a fixed-graph response program. More generally, positive-lag terminality collapses the envelope to the adjustment contrast whenever no admissible bidirected endpoint paired with \(Y_0\) belongs to the reflexive bounded-window ancestry of the controlled possible-parent set; this exact micro condition permits summary cycles through \(Y\) and may hold even when \(Y\) is bidirected with a summary ancestor.
